entry.title: Minimal model of a Plateau-Rayleigh instability of a solid binary alloy nanowire: impacts of surface segregation
entry.summary:
Minimal model and its linear stability analysis (LSA) for Plateau-Rayleigh (PR) instability of an intermixed, solid binary alloy nanowire is presented. Model accounts only for the surface diffusions of the alloy components without anisotropies of a surface energies, and for a classical thermodynamic surface segregation. Model allows to assess a deviation of a longwave instability cutoff wavelength $λ_c$ from the classical value $2πr_0$ (a wire circumference) as a function of a surface composition deviation from its equilibrium value, a wire radius, and a bulk concentration of a minority component.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #materials-science #clean-tech

entry.title: The Merck/Moderna Results
entry.summary:
This is one of those times - and there are many - when you should evaluate a biopharma news story based on the science and not on the stock market. I’m referring to the clinical trial data that Merck and Moderna released yesterday for their vaccine (intismeran autogene)/Keytruda combination in melanoma patients after surgery. That should probably read “released under duress”, because the data leaked in advance of a meeting presentation, and the companies were more or less forced to press-release on the numbers.

Source: In the Pipeline (Derek Lowe — Drug Discovery & Chemistry) · Tags: #genomics-proteins #materials-science

entry.title: Machine learning dataset and benchmark for accurate T cell receptor–pHLA binding prediction
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01073-y Hi-TPH is a large-scale hierarchical dataset that enables more accurate prediction of T cell receptor binding to antigens using protein language models and reveals how molecular components jointly contribute to prediction.

entry.summary:

entry.title: Structure-coefficient theorem for evolutionary games on dynamic networks
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01068-9 The authors establish a structure-coefficient theorem, showing that three universal coefficients capture evolutionary outcomes in changing networks, and identify dynamic core–periphery networks that promote cooperation, altruism, fairness and trust.

entry.title: Hybrid modeling for improved structure prediction of large protein complexes
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01067-w An automated framework, HDOCK-Multimer (HDM), is developed that integrates ab initio docking and combinatorial assembly for the structure prediction of large protein complexes. Across three benchmarks, HDM demonstrates increased accuracy and robustness in modeling large protein assemblies, compared with state-of-the-art…
